title: TraceFlow: Efficient Trace Analysis for Large-Scale Parallel Applications via Interaction Pattern-Aware Trace Distribution
problem: Large-scale trace analysis must handle vast datasets; current parallel trace analysis introduces inter-process communications to fetch non-local event data, causing bottlenecks
motivation: Understanding parallel application interaction behaviors (synchronization, async overlaps) is critical for optimization; trace size explodes with scale; communication overhead limits analysis speed
method: TraceFlow performs static program analysis on the source code beforehand to identify interaction patterns—which parts of the program communicate with each other. Based on this understanding, it partitions trace events so that events from interacting parts are assigned to the same analysis process. This strategy eliminates the inter-process communication that normally bottlenecks large-scale trace analysis.
key_novelty: Static program analysis enables communication-free trace analysis by directing related trace events to the same process based on code interaction patterns.
contributions: Static program structure analysis for partitioning
13.49x average speedup vs state-of-the-art on up to 8192 processes
limitations: Overhead of static analysis phase not detailed; applicability to irregular communication patterns unclear
primary_theme: Efficient large-scale trace analysis via communication minimization
